The treated wastewaters from gas liquors, domestic sewage, and the boiler blowdown water may be used as part of the makeup water for the evaporative cooling water systems. The cooling systems, which lose water by evaporation, account for about 50 percent of the water consumption in the gasification process. Since these cooling water systems are of the recirculating type, they must be blown down periodically to prevent excessive build-up of dissolved solids.
This cooling tower blowdown water, along with blowdown from the softener and demineralizer equipment, may be used to quench ash from the gasifier reactors and to transfer it in a slurry form to the dewatering equipment. The ash can then be dewatered and transported to the mine or other disposal site, while the wastewater may then be transferred to evaporation ponds. About 15 to 20 percent of the water is used in ash disposal. The remaining 30 to 35 percent is converted to steam used by the process chemical reactions as a hydrogen source for manufacture of synthetic gas.
Furnace and fly ash, as well as waste sludge material from raw water, sewage waste and gas liquor treatment processes, could be returned to the mine site for disposal by burial. Due to the possibility of ground water contamination, extreme care must be exercised with this method of disposal to insure that the toxic materials in the ash and sludge will be adequately contained.
